texts: On day 3 of Year 1, Keepers lit the lanterns of the East Row at sundown.
Many nightmoths gathered at the lanterns of the East Row.
The nightmoths landed on the lanterns.
The nightmoths left silken threads on the lanterns.
Pell collected the silken threads from the lanterns at dawn on day 4 of Year 1.
Pell carried the silken threads to Cauldron Hall.
Hesper boiled the silken threads in sea-water in the second cauldron on day 4 of Year 1.
Mire-essence formed in the second cauldron by evening.
Hesper stored the mire-essence in two clay vessels.
Keepers lit the lanterns of the East Row with the stored mire-essence at sundown on day 4 of Year 1.

parse: (: s13_light_rule (Implication (PartOf $x sk_keeper_2) (And (Member (sk_light2 $x) light) (Agent (sk_light2 $x) $x) (Patient (sk_light2 $x) sk_lantern_1) (Instrument (sk_light2 $x) sk_essence_1) (Time (sk_light2 $x) sundown) (Time (sk_light2 $x) (Day 4)) (Time (sk_light2 $x) (Year 1)) (Past (sk_light2 $x)))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

q1_issues.issue: 'left silken threads on the lanterns' deposits the threads unchanged, so the object-change test gives Theme, not Patient — the same threads take Theme under collect / carry / store elsewhere in this parse.
The per-member distribution rule repeats the same mis-assigned Patient role for each nightmoth.
(Ordinal sk_cauldron_1 2 cauldron) fills the scale slot with the entity's own class word, but 'the second cauldron' states no ordering event and no '-est' dimension for that slot.

q2_gaps: Capitalized bare-plural role label ('Keepers lit the lanterns'): the capitalized-common-noun default is declared singular-collective only, and the plural carve-out covers only a label that refers as a name, so a capitalized plural used as an ordinary kind word falls between the two rules.

An ordinal used as a bare identifying label within a fixed set ('the second cauldron', 'the second vat') — no event or dimension is stated to fill Ordinal's scale slot, and the reserved 'unspecified' symbol is licensed only in Measure-family slots.

Bare MASS-noun arguments in episodic clauses ('the lanterns burned mire-essence', 'produced mist-light', 'Mire-essence formed in the second cauldron'): the instruction set states the bare-PLURAL rule (group witness when the set takes part in the occurrence, bare kind filler when non-specific) but gives no mass analog, so the same noun can land on a bare kind or on a witness.

Distributing a transitive predicate whose object is a definite plural group: the per-member rule replicates the whole object group, so 'Keepers lit the lanterns of the East Row' derives that each keeper lit every lantern — there is no object-side under-distribution form ('between them').
review.notes: Coreference chains, calendar/day-part Time terms, compound decomposition (mire_essence, mist_light, nightmoth, silken_thread, sea_water, clay_vessel), group/cardinality handling and truth values are otherwise clean and consistent across all thirteen sentences. Two borderline calls left unflagged: (Instrument sk_boil_1 sea_water) for the surface 'in sea-water' medium PP (defensible under Instrument's 'substance' licence, though Location/In compete), and the split treatment of bare mass arguments — mire_essence as a bare kind at s2 but sk_mistlight_1 / sk_essence_1 as witnesses at s3 / s11.

issues.reason: Thematic roles gives Patient only to an object the action creates, destroys, consumes or physically changes, and threads left on a lantern are deposited unaltered, so the yes/no change test — and its stated 'when the test is unclear, default to Theme' — selects (Theme sk_leave_1 sk_thread_1).
The s7_leave_rule conclusion carries the identical (Patient (sk_leave $x) sk_thread_1) conjunct, so the same unlicensed change-of-state claim is asserted once per nightmoth.

Comparatives & degree defines Ordinal's third slot as the ordering scale — the associated event ((Ordinal priya 1 respond)) or an explicit -est dimension ((Ordinal x 3 tall)) — so filling it with the entity's own class word invents a scale no word supplies and, under the stated 'superlative is the rank-1 special case' reading, yields the ill-typed (Most cauldron ...).

gaps_confirmed: Capitalized bare-plural kind word used as an ordinary role label ('Keepers lit the lanterns'): the capitalized-common-noun default is declared singular-collective only and the plural carve-out covers only a label referring as a name, so no test decides between a Name-only individual and an ordinary bare-plural group witness.

An ordinal used as a bare identifying label inside a fixed set ('the second cauldron'): no event and no -est dimension is stated to fill Ordinal's scale slot, and the reserved 'unspecified' filler is licensed only in Measure-family slots, so the construction has no licensed form at all.

Bare MASS-noun arguments in episodic clauses ('burned mire-essence', 'produced mist-light', 'Mire-essence formed in the second cauldron'): the bare-PLURAL rule states when a participating set takes a group witness versus a bare kind filler, but there is no mass analog, so the same noun can land on either.

No object-side under-distribution form: the per-member rule replicates the whole object (a definite plural group or a shared singular witness), so 'Keepers lit the lanterns of the East Row' derives that each keeper lit every lantern, and the instruction set offers no 'between them' shape to weaken it.
new_gaps: Day-of-year dating in a month-less calendar ('on day 3 of Year 1'): the Time term (Day <n>) is defined as day-of-month (June 5, 2021 -> (Day 5)), so a day counted within a year has no distinct carrier and the Day+Year pair emitted here is indistinguishable from a day-of-month reading — which also leaves the seeded date-ordering rules (year, same-year month, same-year-month day) unable to order day 3 before day 4.

Verb/noun homograph collapse: lemmatization maps every surface form of a word to one symbol with no sense slot, so 'lit' and the head noun of 'mist-light' both land on `light` — this parse holds (Member sk_light_1 light) for the lighting event beside (Inheritance mist_light light) for the substance, and any rule or query over `light` conflates the two.
adjudication.defect_summary: The compliant form for s7_leave_pat is (Theme sk_leave_1 sk_thread_1); the compliant form for s7_leave_rule is the same rule with (Theme (sk_leave $x) sk_thread_1) in the conclusion; for 'the second cauldron' NO compliant form is licensed — Ordinal's scale slot admits only an associated event or an explicit -est dimension and `unspecified` is barred outside Measure-family slots, so the only rule-conforming output is (Member sk_cauldron_1 cauldron) with the ordinal label dropped and recorded as the gap above.
adjudication.notes: The s1 and s13 per-member rules instantiate the reviewer's fourth gap as an actual over-assertion — each keeper is derived to have lit the entire lantern group — and s3's rule does the same with the single mist-light witness. The mire_essence bare-kind / witness split the reviewer notes in passing is defensible rather than defective: s3 and s11 mint witnesses precisely because later definite mentions corefer with them, while s2's object is the non-specific kind filler the 'grows wheat' clause licenses.
